summary: Genuine counter-evidence search attempted for all 5 target claims per their specific search angles. Claim 2 (Lent/Easter calendar-timing outperformance) and claim 4 (referral LTV/trust stats) turned up strong, source-diverse counter-evidence: claim 2's Feb 2024 spike coincides with a rare Ash-Wednesday/Super-Bowl calendar confluence (first since 2008) plus a documented 15x paid-spend increase and celebrity ad, undercutting attribution to calendar timing alone; claim 4's '~25% LTV' figure traces to a real peer-reviewed study (Schmitt/Skiera/Van den Bulte 2011) but its '83% trust' figure appears to conflate an unrelated general Nielsen word-of-mouth-trust statistic, and independent commentary documents real referral-program failure modes (quality abuse, channel cannibalization) that qualify the 'dominant proven pattern' framing. Claim 1 (parish partnerships) yielded a plausible structural counter-mechanism (Catholic dioceses have centralized parish-management infrastructure that Protestant/non-denominational churches lack) but the '30% user increase' figure itself remains untraceable to any primary data after a genuine search -- reported as a traceability gap. Claim 3 (authenticity vs. production) is best supported by an internal contradiction within the brief's own sourcing (Wahlberg Super Bowl ad vs. authenticity claim) plus reinforced suspicion of vendor-narrative bias, since external sources found were in the same commercially-interested agency category as the original claim's sources; no disinterested empirical study directly resolving the question was found. Claim 5 (scale-dependent tactics transferring to a small group/study product) found no niche-specific counter-evidence -- the closest comparable, SmartGroups, has no public growth story -- so only adjacent-category general startup-positioning-risk material was found; this is reported as an unresolved, still-open extrapolation risk rather than a settled finding in either direction, consistent with the plan's own framing of this as the brief's biggest structural risk.
